image: You sit down with them and no one asks why you came.
A single lamp over the bench.
The low sun comes in under the cloud, and every stone on the moor has a shadow.
The lagoon water clears for a moment and something below stirs, then closes over again.
You water the cutting and then leave it alone.
The rowan feeds the thrush, and the thrush carries its seed over the hill.
You lift the end no one else could get under, and it comes up.
You stand by your word though it costs you your sleep.
The cow is sold in the autumn, and what she fetched carries the household through the winter.
The milk spills over the brim of the pail.
In the sunshine you can see where you stand on the slope.
The sun finally reaches into the valley and everything goes still.
An unnamed voice memo sits in your phone, three minutes long.
Out on the heath a twig snaps, and the whole party goes quiet to listen.
The turf wall the forefathers built now sinks slowly back into the earth.
The salmon throws itself at the falls again.
After the storm, only the tree with deep roots is still standing.
From the pass you look back, and your tracks in the snow make one line down the valley.
The door swollen by rain opens at the third push of your shoulder.
The plant on the sill turns itself flat to the glass, toward the one hour of light it gets.
The calm lies over the fjord and nothing stirs, not even the bird on the rock.
One minute of hail, and the tulips are lying on the path.
